cards.b: A nibble is 4 bits; a byte is 8 bits.

cards.f: How many values can n bits store?
cards.b: 2ⁿ different values. 8 bits give 256 values (0 to 255).
Split into nibbles of 4 bits (from the right). Each nibble is one hex digit, e.g. 1100 1011 = CB.
It is shorter than binary, so easier to read and remember, and less likely to be mistyped. It converts easily to and from binary.
Colour codes in HTML/CSS, MAC addresses, IPv6 addresses, error codes, memory dumps, URLs.
The result of a calculation is too large to store in the available bits, e.g. an 8-bit addition that needs a ninth bit.
Bits move n places left, 0s fill the right, bits fall off the left. The number is multiplied by 2ⁿ.
Bits move n places right, 0s fill the left. The number is divided by 2ⁿ and the remainder is lost.
If a 1 is shifted off the end, the answer is wrong (left) or truncated (right).
In 8 bits the left-hand bit has the value −128 instead of +128. Left bit 1 means a negative number.
Write the positive number in 8 bits, invert every bit, then add 1.

short.q: Add 10110110 and 00101101 as 8-bit numbers. Show the result and check it in denary.
short.model: 10110110 + 00101101 = 11100011. In denary 182 + 45 = 227, which is 128+64+32+2+1, so it fits in 8 bits and there is no overflow.

short.q: Shift 10100000 right by 2 places. Give the result and its effect on the value.
short.model: The result is 00101000. The value goes from 160 to 40, so it is divided by 4 (2²).

short.q: Shift 11000000 left by 1 place in an 8-bit register. Explain why the answer is wrong.
short.model: The result is 10000000 (128), but 192 × 2 = 384. The leading 1 is shifted off the left end and lost, so the answer is wrong.
points: a 1 is lost / shifted off the end
